back: Charging all costs to products: direct costs plus a share of overheads absorbed on a stated basis (units or labour hours).
Overhead absorption rate = total overheads ÷ total units (or labour hours). Overhead absorbed = rate × the product's units (or hours).
Full cost per unit = direct cost per unit + overhead absorbed per unit. Price with mark-up = cost × (1 + mark-up %).
Selling price per unit minus variable cost per unit; the amount each unit adds towards fixed costs and profit.
Profit = total contribution - fixed costs. Total contribution = contribution per unit × units sold.
The basis for absorbing overheads is arbitrary; overheads are fixed; it can reject worthwhile orders; relies on forecast output.
Special orders, keeping or dropping a product, short-term pricing, choosing between products, break-even and budgeting.
Price above variable cost, spare capacity, no loss of normal sales, no extra fixed costs and no pressure on regular prices.
Full costing for regular prices and long-run cost recovery; contribution costing for short-term decisions where fixed costs are already committed.
